title: Why Victorian Children Were Forced to Climb Chimneys
description:
In February 1875, a twelve-year-old boy named George Brewster died wedged in a chimney flue in Cambridge. His death ended a trade that Parliament had been trying — and failing — to stop for nearly a century: the use of child 'climbing boys' to sweep Britain's chimneys. This episode follows the apprenticeships, the flues, the tools, the soot cancer first identified in 1775, and the sixty years of laws that changed nothing until someone was paid to enforce them.

Disclosure: This video is an animated reconstruction made with AI/synthetic tools — the narration is a synthetic voice, and all visuals are code-drawn flat-vector illustrations. The character 'Thomas' is a reconstructed composite based on documented climbing boys' testimonies, not a real individual; scenes featuring him are illustration, not evidence.
